message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Windows command line

The simplest way to terminate all running VS Code windows (and any child processes it may have spawned) is to use the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

#### What the switches mean

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Kill by **image name** (process name). Here we target `code.exe`. |
| `/F`   | **Force** the termination (equivalent to `Ctrl‑C` + `Ctrl‑Break`). |
| `/T`   | (Optional) Also terminate **child processes** of the target. Useful if VS Code has spawned helper processes that you also want to close. |

So a more thorough command would be:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

---

### If you only want to kill a specific instance

1. Find the Process ID (PID) first:

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

   This will list all `code.exe` instances along with their PIDs.

2. Kill the desired PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
   ```

   Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number you saw in the previous step.

---

### Using PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <PID_NUMBER> -Force
```

---

### Quick recap

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Kill **all** VS Code windows | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` |
| Kill **all** VS Code windows + children | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |
| Kill a **specific** instance | `taskkill /PID <PID> /F` |
| PowerShell equivalent | `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` |

> **Tip:** If you’re running into “Access denied” errors, try launching the command prompt or PowerShell as **Administrator**.

That’s it! Use the appropriate command depending on whether you want to close every VS Code instance or just a particular one.
